3	  "body": "Fixes [NIW2-604](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-604). The owner reported it with screenshots.

## What was wrong
In "Check and fix files", a slightly off-target press on a row's checkbox expanded the row (the note wrapped to two lines), and the checkbox didn't toggle.

The cause was `.row:focus-within`, which un-truncated the row's text.
1. A mousedown on the box focused it.
2. The row reflowed taller, and the 16 px box moved out from under the cursor.
3. The mouseup landed off the input, so no `click` fired and nothing toggled.
4. The row stayed expanded for as long as focus remained.

## Fix
- Row text expands only for keyboard focus: `.row:has(:focus-visible)`. A mouse press no longer changes the layout under the cursor.
- A click anywhere on a selectable row toggles it (`cursor: pointer`). The box's own click still toggles exactly once.

## Verification
- A new test clicks the row's padding and its text, then the box itself. All three toggle, and each toggles once.
- The reconcile suite passes (15 tests), as do the web typecheck, oxlint and oxfmt.
- Electron was not launched on this machine.

## How to test it yourself
1. Settings → Workspaces → **Check and fix files** on a library that has findings, then expand a group.
2. Press just beside a row's checkbox, or on its text. The row toggles, and nothing expands or jumps.
3. Press the checkbox itself. It toggles once.
4. Tab to a row's checkbox with the keyboard. The full name and note show, wrapped.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

findings.title: Double-clicking a name to copy it still toggles the row once
findings.body: The guard covers a drag-select, but not a double- or triple-click, which is the other common way to select a name. In Chromium the first click's `click` fires while nothing is selected yet, so line 217 toggles the row. The word only gets selected on the second mousedown, so only the second `click` is skipped. The net result is one toggle plus a selection, which is the same side effect the earlier thread described. Two possible fixes: on the row's `onMouseDown`, call `preventDefault()` when `event.detail > 1` (but that blocks word selection), or compare `event.detail` and undo the first toggle when `detail === 2`. If double-click copying isn't a goal, a comment saying so would be enough.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed. Line 216 skips the toggle when there's a selection, so a drag-select over a name no longer flips the row. The test at reconcile.test.tsx:368-374 covers it. One small remaining case: a double-click to select a name still toggles on its first click. I've filed that as a separate consider.

input.summary: The fix does what the reply on the earlier thread says. The row's click handler now returns early when the window has a text selection, so a drag-select over a name to copy it no longer toggles the row. Clicks on the checkbox itself are still handled on their own path. The test mocks `getSelection` and checks that the box keeps its state, so I'm closing the earlier thread as addressed. One case is still open, filed as a consider: a double-click to select a name toggles the row on its first click, because the word only gets selected on the second mousedown.
